newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese judiciary declares war on corruption.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese judiciary declares war on corruption.

text.p: Lebanese judicial authorities have declared war on corruption after media reports of financial scandals in public institutions, Beirut's senior prosecutor general was quoted on Monday as saying.

Prosecutor-general Adnan Addoum told the daily newspaper as-Safir the judicial year, which began in September, "will be devoted entirely to fighting corruption in public institutions in all its forms, including receiving bribes".

"Just as we succeeded last year in ending the drugs trade in Lebanon, we will succeed this year in putting an end to the issue of corruption," he said, adding that suspects would be investigated "without waiting for anyone's permission".
Beirut newspapers have recently reported cases of alleged corruption, including embezzlement of funds, in some government ministries and state institutions.
Billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri said on Monday judicial authorities were investigating some cases and charges of alleged corruption.

"A lot of dust is being stirred up about corruption in the administration aiming at saying the whole system is corrupt. There are cases and charges that the judiciary and concerned councils are investigating and they may prove to be right or baseless," Hariri said in a speech.
